The International Day of Charity is observed every year on September 5. It was established by the United Nations to promote and recognize charity and its important role in alleviating humanitarian crises and human suffering, as well as in promoting solidarity and social bonding. Charity has played a vital role throughout history in meeting the needs of the most vulnerable societies around the world. The International Day of Charity aims to strengthen this spirit and remind people and organizations of their social responsibility.

• September 5 (marks the anniversary of the death of Mother Teresa, renowned for her charitable work)
• Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2012
• Raise awareness and encourage individuals, NGOs, and organizations to help others through volunteer and philanthropic activities.

Observance:
• People commemorate the day through donations, volunteering, community service, and organizing events or campaigns to support various causes.
• Many governments, civil society organizations, and communities participate and organize events to raise public
